entrypoints.summary: The TCP-served wrapper reads submitted program lines through standard input until a line beginning with __EOF__, accepts at most 512 bytes, and inserts the resulting text into a Rust main function.
socat exposes python3 app.py on TCP port 1337.

affected_components.role: Reads attacker text, substitutes FLAG and submitted text into a temporary Rust file, invokes rustc, and emits the exit-status marker.
Organizer payload performs CTFE source-byte searching and drives prefix enumeration.

code_slices.fixed: No fixed implementation or patch is present in the bundle.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The organizer payload exits main, evaluates a static const expression, reads its own generated source with include_bytes!(file!()), and forces compilation failure when a selected query is absent.
code_slices.vulnerable: The wrapper substitutes FLAG and attacker program text into one Rust template, writes it to a temporary .rs file, runs rustc, and exposes only its exit-status class.

negative_controls: timeout is retried by the supplied solver rather than treated as a query result.
observability.positive_marker: :) indicates rustc returned zero for the submitted query.

preconditions: Service deployment provides FLAG to the wrapper environment and exposes TCP port 1337.
Attacker input is inserted into the generated Rust source and rustc accepts compile-time include_bytes! evaluation in this environment.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Rust source fragment containing a selected candidate query, a const function over included source bytes, and assert!(false) for a nonmatch.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit a payload that closes the generated main function and installs a static const-evaluation substring test over include_bytes!(file!()).

trigger_steps.payload_shape: One query per candidate prefix from an alphabet of closing brace, underscore, lowercase letters, and digits.
trigger_steps.summary: Repeat requests while appending each candidate character to a known prefix, retaining the character for which the service reports successful compilation.

capabilities.concept: compile-time reading of generated compilation-unit bytes

mitigations.concept: exclude secrets from attacker-influenced compilation units

relation_candidates.dst: compile-time reading of generated compilation-unit bytes
relation_candidates.rationale: The wrapper embeds submitted text in the same Rust unit, and the supplied payload invokes include_bytes!(file!()) during const evaluation.
The payload searches the included source for a chosen byte query and causes const-evaluation failure when absent, while the wrapper exposes rustc status.
relation_candidates.src: compile-time reading of generated compilation-unit bytes

relation_candidates.rationale: The supplied solver treats ':)' as a positive query result and enumerates allowed next characters until a closing brace is found.
The solver begins with SECCON{ and appends characters selected by the status oracle before printing the recovered flag.

relation_candidates.dst: exclude secrets from attacker-influenced compilation units
relation_candidates.rationale: Keeping the secret out of the generated source removes the secret-bearing file content used by the included-byte search.
relation_candidates.src: compile-time reading of generated compilation-unit bytes

impact.affected_asset: FLAG value injected into the sandbox service configuration.
impact.attacker_capability: Select candidate FLAG prefixes and distinguish matching from nonmatching candidates by the service response.
impact.security_effect: Disclosure of the FLAG through an adaptive compiler-status side channel without needing to execute a compiled attacker binary.

causal_trace.summary: A remote client supplies up to 512 bytes of Rust program text, terminated by an __EOF__ marker, which the wrapper interpolates into a Rust source template.
The wrapper removes FLAG from its own environment but substitutes its value into a comment in the temporary Rust compilation unit that also contains attacker-controlled text.

The organizer solver closes the template's main function and uses a static const-evaluation expression whose include_bytes!(file!()) reads the generated source; its byte substring search asserts false when an attacker-selected query is absent.

The service maps rustc exit status to ':)' or ':(' while suppressing compiler output; the supplied solver adaptively tests successive FLAG prefixes using that result, yielding a secret-dependent compilation-status oracle.

failure.operation: Rust compile-time evaluation reads the generated source through include_bytes!(file!()) and converts substring membership into a compile success/failure condition.

primary_invariant.kind: secret isolation across compilation units and compiler outcomes
primary_invariant.statement: A secret must not be present in an attacker-influenced compilation unit or influence an externally observable compilation result.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The generated Rust source contains the substituted FLAG, and attacker-controlled Rust can use compile-time file inclusion and a const assertion to make rustc success depend on whether a guessed secret substring occurs in that source.

quality.review_notes: Primary wrapper and organizer solver were inspected and establish the mechanism and intended adaptive oracle. The bundle contains deployment material and solver code but no captured independent execution transcript or test result, so reproducibility is not asserted as observed. No organizer remediation patch is supplied; mitigation is an invariant-restoring reconstruction.

remediation.invariant_restored: Do not render secrets into any source file compiled with attacker-controlled content, and ensure externally reported compiler success, failure, and timing do not depend on secret-derived source data.

target.language: Python wrapper and Rust submitted source
